q: Pick the correct one

options.A: Upto Rs.50,000/- through any of the available suppliers on the GeM, meeting the requisite quality, specification and delivery period.
options.B: Above Rs.50,000/- and upto Rs.10,00,000/- through GeM seller having lowest price amongst the available sellers , of at least three different manufacturers, on GeM ,meeting the requisite quality , specification and delivery period.
options.C: Above Rs.10,00,000/- through the supplier having lowest price meeting the requisite quality, specification and delivery period after mandatorily obtaining bids, using online bidding or reverse auction tool provided on GeM.
options.D: All of the above are correct

e: All three statements are correct under GFR Rule 149 as amended: direct purchase on GeM is allowed up to Rs.50,000; above Rs.50,000 and up to Rs.10,00,000 the purchase is made through the lowest-priced seller among at least three different manufacturers; and above Rs.10,00,000 bids must be obtained mandatorily using online bidding or the reverse auction tool provided on GeM. (Source: Department of Expenditure compilation of GFR amendments up to 31.07.2024, quoting Rule 149 as amended on 10.07.2024.)

q: Proprietary Article Certificate is applicable in
e: The correct answer is Single Tender Enquiry. Option (C) is correct: the Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC) is applicable in Single Tender Enquiry. A PAC certifies that the required item is proprietary to one specific firm and can be obtained from no other source, which justifies inviting only that firm instead of open competition. A related exam fact: for purchases above Rs.25 lakhs the PAC must be signed by the PHOD/CHOD.

q: What does EMD stand for ?

It is the security amount deposited by a bidder along with the tender to show serious intent, and it discourages frivolous bids. A related exam fact: EMD of unsuccessful bidders is refunded after finalisation, while the maximum EMD leviable is Rs.50 lakhs irrespective of tender value. This provision exists for a practical reason in day-to-day railway working; keeping that practical picture in mind makes the fact far easier to retain than memorising it in isolation.

q: What does CRAC stand for ?

q: IGST is payable when the supply is
e: The correct answer is Interstate. Option (A) is correct: IGST is payable when the supply is inter-state, i.e. the supplier and the recipient are in different states. GST is a destination-based tax, so tax on inter-state movement of goods or services goes to the Centre as IGST. A related exam fact: on intra-state supplies, CGST and SGST are levied together instead of IGST. A useful way to verify this in the exam hall is to ask what would break if the opposite were true — the logic of the underlying system points straight to this option.

q: What are the taxes levied on intra-state Supply ?
e: Option (C) is correct: on intra-state supplies both CGST (Central GST) and SGST (State GST) are levied, roughly splitting the total GST between the Centre and the State. This dual levy is the core of India's GST design for supplies within a state. This is a concept-clarity question. q: GST stands for

e: The correct answer is 1 Jul 2017. Option (A) is correct: GST was implemented in India on 1 July 2017, subsuming taxes like excise duty, service tax and VAT into one national tax. q: What is the maximum rate of CGST prescribed under GST ACT 2017?
e: The maximum rate of CGST prescribed under the CGST Act is 20% — Section 9 of the CGST Act, 2017 caps the central tax at 20% (the SGST Act carries the same 20% cap, so the combined ceiling is 40%). The notified slab rates (now 5% merit / 18% standard, with a 40% de-merit total rate on specified goods) are different from this statutory ceiling for CGST alone.

q: GST is a ______ based tax on consumption of goods & services
e: Option (C) is correct: GST is a destination-based tax on the consumption of goods and services, meaning tax accrues to the state where the goods or services are finally consumed, not where they are produced. This is why IGST applies on inter-state supplies. This is a concept-clarity question.
